svg.text: libaudition — development roadmap
Proposed technical milestones · version labels are not release commitments · 23 Oct 2026
Full work-item graph and dependencies are available in development_roadmap.mmd
M0 — Release baseline
P0
• Verify the exact release commit against the full CI matrix (Linux, macOS, sanitizers, optional backends)
• Freeze and document public C++17 contracts: AudioView, timestamps, clock domains, source and speaker IDs, uncertainty
• Validate CMake install/export, static/shared consumers, third-party notices and model provenance
• Document unsupported deployment claims and decide whether the release candidate can be tagged
Gate: Exact-commit CI and independent installed consumer pass; exclusions and licenses recorded.
M1 — Reusable signal processing
P0
• Provide FFT/IFFT plans, real/complex transforms, frequency-bin conventions and documented scaling
• Add Hann/Hamming/Blackman windows and streaming STFT/ISTFT with defined reconstruction and latency
• Provide FIR/IIR/biquad filters, high-order fractional delay and explicit reset/flush behavior
• Expose spectral features: PSD, log-mel, MFCC, spectral flux, onset, pitch and harmonicity
• Add calibrated A/C weighting, noise-floor estimation and separately configurable AGC, gate and limiter
Gate: Independent numerical references, reconstruction tolerances, chunk/reset tests and memory bounds.
M2 — Streaming and source lifecycle
P0
• Instrument per-channel levels, clipping, dropout, timestamp drift and capture-to-inference delays
• Introduce adaptive noise-floor estimation, onset thresholds, hysteresis, debounce and expiry tuning
• Specify source states: tentative, confirmed, inactive, lost and retired; prevent stale spatial tracks
• Harden per-source PCM epochs, backpressure, source retirement, late ASR results and ID reuse
• Keep spatial PCM phase-consistent; apply AEC/noise reduction/AGC on an explicit speech branch
Gate: Quiet/short-source corpus regressions; no stale tracks or source contamination; bounded queues.
M3 — Spatial algorithms and tracking
P1
• Version microphone-array geometry and measured gain, phase and delay calibration profiles
• Implement pluggable GCC-PHAT, SRP-PHAT and MUSIC localization baselines alongside ODAS
• Implement delay-and-sum beamforming; evaluate MVDR with numerical conditioning constraints
• Evaluate multiple-source association, covariance, split/merge and persistent acoustic-source re-ID
• Compare configurations on annotated stationary/moving sources, reverberation and overlap
Gate: Reproducible angular error, detection/track continuity and separation metrics against ODAS baseline.
M4 — Speech and speaker processing
P1
• Evaluate far-field AEC3, denoising, resampling and speech-path level control using playback references
• Validate VAD segmentation, pre/post-roll and offline/streaming ASR under low-SNR and overlap
• Validate token/word timestamps, language identification, KWS and source-bound partial/final results
• Evaluate speaker embeddings, verification, diarization and enrolled/unknown speaker decisions
• Document TTS interruption, playback echo interactions and model-specific capability restrictions
Gate: Measured WER, DER, keyword false alarms, AEC ERLE and source association on held-out recordings.
M5 — Semantic events and acoustic memory
P1
• Benchmark YAMNet, EfficientAT, CLAP and sherpa with matched audio windows and label mappings
• Separate raw scores from calibrated probabilities and validate unknown/open-vocabulary rejection
• Extend temporal events, DTW, recurrence and motifs to recurring source-local acoustic patterns
• Develop versioned sound prototypes, novelty detection and controlled long-term source memory
• Expose source/event observations with provenance, uncertainty and explicit event lifecycles
Gate: Held-out event F1/mAP, false-alarm rate, novelty and source-memory contamination measured.
M6 — Developer SDK and deployment
P1–P2
• Provide concise recipes for classification, source tracking, speech transcription and replay
• Maintain stable low-level C++ contracts; evaluate optional C and Python bindings
• Profile queue bounds, allocation/lock behavior, p50/p95/p99 latency and multi-source load
• Benchmark optimized CPU paths (AVX/NEON) and optional inference providers (OpenVINO/RKNN/CUDA)
• Publish install guides, samples, feature maturity matrix and reproducible package profiles
Gate: Independent consumer build and documented measured runtime/memory profile for supported targets.
Cross-cutting quality and benchmarking (P0)
• Maintain dataset/model manifests (SHA-256, licensing, geometry, sample rate, annotations).
• Distinguish deterministic unit tests, model smoke, annotated benchmarks and physical HIL.
• Record representative multi-channel scenes: silence, faint/brief speech, moving sources, 1/2/5/10 sources.
• Measure task metrics: DOA error, ID switches, WER, DER, classification F1/mAP and AEC ERLE.
• Record runtime p50/p95/p99, throughput, RAM, alloc count, drops and power by platform.
• Establish baseline-relative regression limits; skipped external corpora are not passes.
Optional research (not required for release)
Acoustic mapping · synchronized arrays · predictive events · continual adaptation · auditory attention and privacy
